1950, March 15
The following is a faithful transcription of the typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O.P.M. Cap.
SAINT FELIX FRIARY. HUNTINGTON, INDIATA
March 15th 1950.
Ven. Sister Mary Constance, O.P.
Dear Sister Mary Constance: God bless you and may He be your Stay , your Refuge and your divine Guide these days. I have hoped that by enc- couraging you as I have been trying to do these several months, that with the many prayers that I know are being offered for your guidance,- your conversion indeed - you might, by cooperating with God's holy grace, be fully convinced that your only salvation, for time as well as for eternity, is a generous and whole-hearted sacrifice of your --- your everything to God.
Your desperate experiences these same months (hair-breadthly border- ering on fearful tragedy), -- experiences -- inthemselves and in reality extraordinary manifestations of God's mercy to you Sister Mary Constance, -- which ought surely to help convince you that such is about the only con- clusion for you to come to.
While I have still more than hope that during these fearful experiences, you have not strayed mortal-sinfully from your Rule; nevertheless I believe on the other hand that, had you been really faith- ful to your vows and absolutely turned down the promises and the allure- ments of the world, the flesh and the devil as you should have done (two years ago), God would have promoted you before this to an incalculably more intimate and happy confidence and espousals with the divien Lover of Souls - to something vastly surpassing your highest ideal.
You have lost out fearfully Sister: but your mistake is not irrepar- able. By the mercy of God and your humble and grateful cooperation therewith, you can, not-only regain your former standing in the Hearts of Jesus and Mary; but like St. Paul who from even a zealot persecutor of the Church became an all-surpassing Apotstle, Vessel of election, you too can -- and out of humble gratitude ought to -- become outstanding on the side of Truth and justice in the already-raging warfare against Antichrist and atheism.
Your mistake of seeking solace and peace from other sources than in the Cross and the Crucified, and innumerable lesser mistakes that in consequence have followed since have evidently disturbed and muddled your spiritual waters, to say the least and beclouded your vocational horizon. Otherwise you would hardly moralize with so many "ifs" and "whys" and we might say "half truths." Yes, love in itself is always beauti- ful, but when and inasmuch as even love becomes inordinate it loses that native beauty and like an immortal soul in sin, becomes hedious in the sight of God and Heven. Illegitimate love is always inordinate; not always visa versa. Here is an actual example of the latter:
